$comment: Findings of tools/priv-scan.mjs that a person has looked at and cleared. History is not rewritten to clear a canary, so this is the only way a commit that has already reached `main` stops being reported. AN EXEMPTION THAT MATCHES NOTHING FAILS: the scan goes red naming any entry here that its walk does not reproduce, which is what stops this file accumulating entries for findings that no longer exist and stops it being used to pre-authorise a shape nobody has seen. Each entry is {commit, where, code, reason}; `commit` may be a prefix of at least seven hex characters, `where` is a repository path or the literal `commit-message`, and `code` is the finding's code exactly as the scan printed it.
$comment_empty: Empty on 2026-09-19, and that is a measurement rather than a default: tools/priv-scan.mjs was run over all 213 commits after this repository's root commit and over the 37 composed documents in them, and found nothing. The two shapes that would otherwise have been in here are exempted by rule instead of by entry, because both recur: git's own authorship trailers (51 of the 53 addresses in the last sixty commit messages are `Co-Authored-By: … <noreply@anthropic.com>`) and RFC 2606 reserved TLDs (`1@evil.example`, a test vector in a commit body about a host parser). An exemption written per-commit for something that happens on every commit is a file that grows for ever and is read by nobody.

exemptions.reason: A fixture identity inside a quoted watched-red transcript. The commit records what B-T0.2's canary printed when the guard was broken on purpose, and the test's stand-in maintainer is called `@the-maintainer`; it names no person and exists only in bot/tests/policy.test.mjs. Exempted by ENTRY and not by rule, deliberately: unlike RFC 2606's reserved names, which are exempted by rule because the address IS the evidence in an e-mail finding, a handle here is decoration inside a quoted block and the transcript reads the same with it elided. So the convention this entry records is to elide identity-shaped values when quoting a transcript, and a second and third occurrence would be the signal that the convention is not holding and the shape wants a rule instead.

The commit that added the exemption above, carrying the same fixture handle twice — once quoting the finding it cleared and once naming the test's stand-in maintainer. Its own entry had just written the convention 'elide identity-shaped values when quoting a transcript', and it broke that convention in the act of recording it. The specific defect is one I had not connected: a PULL REQUEST BODY becomes the squash commit message, so a convention about commit messages is a convention about PR bodies and I wrote neither down as the other. Recorded as a second entry rather than as a rule because the recurrence is self-inflicted — the same author quoting himself minutes later — and the repair is mechanical (check the body before merging) rather than definitional. The next INDEPENDENT occurrence, by somebody who was not quoting this, is the trigger to exempt the shape by rule instead.

Third entry, one root event, and the third time by the same author writing about the first. The cause each time was identical and is now named precisely: I quoted the scan's OWN FINDING LINE verbatim as the evidence. A finding line contains the offending value by construction, so quoting one is guaranteed to reproduce it, and 'elide identity-shaped values' is unfollowable advice while the thing being recorded is the finding itself. The concrete form of the convention, which the two earlier entries lacked and which is what makes it followable: NEVER QUOTE A PRIVACY FINDING'S LINE. Describe it - the code, the commit, and what kind of value it was - and let the scan's own transcript in the run log be the verbatim record. Not repaired by rule, deliberately: a rule that exempted text matching the scan's own report format would create a structured way to write an identity into a commit message unscanned, and PRIV-2's threat is a real person's name in a permanent public record, which such a rule makes cheaper rather than dearer. Three entries about one event is ugly and safe; that trade is the right way round.
